title: Minkä värisiä: asking about several things
summary: For the colours of several things, use minkä värisiä. Minkä värisiä autot ovat? — Autot ovat punaisia.
targetSkills: Minkä värisiä: asking about several things
prerequisiteSkills: Minkä värinen: asking the colour of one thing
objectives: Ask the colours of several things with minkä värisiä.
Answer with the appropriate plural partitive colour form.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which.
For the colours of several things, use minkä värisiä. Minkä stays unchanged, while värinen becomes värisiä. Minkävärisiä is the corresponding joined spelling.
keyPoints: Keep the describing part of the colour question plural, while minkä stays unchanged.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Describe the ordinary plural group's members with a plural partitive colour adjective: Autot ovat punaisia (“The cars are red”). The taught -nen colour words change -nen to -sia/-siä; other supplied patterns include musta → mustia and vihreä → vihreitä.
A natural short reply to “Minkä värisiä autot ovat?” is “Punaisia.” (“Red.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
The complete negative phrase eivät ole is supplied. The plural colour forms remain appropriate when correcting the description of these cars.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use the plural partitive colour form for these groups of separate things.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: punaisia means red here. Punainen changes -nen to -sia: punaisia.
sinisiä means blue here. Sininen changes -nen to -siä: sinisiä.
valkoisia means white here. Valkoinen changes -nen to -sia: valkoisia.
mustia means black here. Musta changes final a to i and adds a: mustia.
vihreitä means green here. Vihreä uses the taught plural stem vihrei- with -tä: vihreitä.
keltaisia means yellow here. Keltainen changes -nen to -sia: keltaisia.
ruskeita means brown here. Ruskea uses the plural stem ruskei- with -ta: ruskeita.

examples.finnish: Autot eivät ole sinisiä. Autot ovat punaisia.
examples.english: The cars are not blue. The cars are red.
steps: Autot: cars; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Auto + plural -t gives autot.
eivät: do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). Eivät is the plural third-person negative verb.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
sinisiä: blue; description of what the subject is like. Sininen changes -nen to -siä: sinisiä.
ovat: are; verb (the action or state). Olla has the irregular plural third-person form ovat.
punaisia: red; description of what the subject is like. Punainen changes -nen to -sia: punaisia.
